_about: One-sentence English summaries and tags for every quatrain, used by find_quatrains for paraphrased searches, plus curated correspondences. The English (FitzGerald) and Persian texts are separate collections: 'related' lists the Persian quatrains an English quatrain draws on, where a correspondence is clear. Several English quatrains have no counterpart in the Persian file and many Persian quatrains have none in FitzGerald.

1.gloss: Dawn: the sun scatters the stars from the field of night and strikes the sultan's tower with light; a call to wake.

2.gloss: Before the false dawn fades, a voice from the tavern asks why the worshipper dozes outside when the temple within is ready.

3.gloss: At cockcrow the crowd at the tavern begs the door to open: our stay is short and once departed we never return.

4.gloss: The New Year revives old desires; the thoughtful soul withdraws to solitude, where spring works miracles like the hand of Moses and the breath of Jesus.

5.gloss: Iram and Jamshyd's seven-ringed cup are gone and forgotten, yet a ruby still glows in the vine and gardens bloom by the water.

6.gloss: David's lips are sealed, but the nightingale sings in old Persian to the rose: wine, red wine, to flush her pale cheek.

7.gloss: Fill the cup and throw off the winter garment of repentance in the fire of spring; the bird of time has little way to fly and is already on the wing.

8.gloss: Whether in Naishapur or Babylon, sweet or bitter, the wine of life keeps dripping away and the leaves of life keep falling one by one.

9.gloss: Each morning brings a thousand roses, but where is yesterday's rose? The same summer month that brings the rose takes kings like Jamshyd and Kaikobad away.

10.gloss: Let time take the kings; what are Kaikobad or Kaikhosru to us? Let Zal and Rustum bluster and Hatim call to supper, and pay no heed.

11.gloss: Come along the green strip between desert and sown, where the names of slave and sultan are forgotten; let Mahmud keep his golden throne.

12.gloss: A book of verses under the bough, a jug of wine, a loaf of bread, and you singing beside me in the wilderness: the wilderness would be paradise enough.

13.gloss: Some chase this world's glories and some sigh for the Prophet's paradise; take the cash in hand, let the credit go, and ignore the distant drum.

14.gloss: The rose laughs as she blows into the world, tears open the silken tassel of her purse and throws her treasure on the garden.

15.gloss: Those who hoarded the golden grain and those who flung it to the winds are alike turned to earth that no one wants to dig up again.

16.gloss: The worldly hope men set their hearts on turns to ashes or prospers, and then like snow on the desert's dusty face is gone within an hour or two.

17.gloss: The world is a battered caravanserai whose doors are night and day, where sultan after sultan with his pomp lodged his destined hour and went his way.

18.gloss: The lion and the lizard keep the courts where Jamshyd gloried and drank; the wild ass stamps over the head of Bahram the hunter and cannot break his sleep.

19.gloss: Perhaps the rose blows reddest where some buried Caesar bled, and every hyacinth the garden wears dropped from some once lovely head.

20.gloss: Lean lightly on the tender green that fledges the river's lip: who knows from what once lovely lip it springs unseen.

21.gloss: Beloved, fill the cup that clears today of past regrets and future fears; tomorrow I may be with yesterday's seven thousand years.

22.gloss: Those we loved best, pressed from his vintage by rolling time, drank their cup a round or two before us and one by one crept silently to rest.

23.gloss: We who now make merry in the room they left must ourselves descend beneath the couch of earth, to make a couch for whom?

24.gloss: Make the most of what we may yet spend before we too descend into dust: dust into dust, under dust to lie, without wine, song, singer or end.

25.gloss: For those who prepare for today and those who stare after some tomorrow alike, a muezzin cries from the tower of darkness: fools, your reward is neither here nor there.

26.gloss: The saints and sages who discussed the two worlds so wisely are thrust forth like foolish prophets; their words are scorned and their mouths stopped with dust.

27.gloss: In youth I eagerly frequented doctor and saint and heard great argument about it and about, but always came out by the same door I went in.

28.gloss: I sowed the seed of wisdom with my own hand and worked to make it grow, and all the harvest I reaped was: I came like water and like wind I go.

29.gloss: Into this universe, not knowing why or whence, like water willy-nilly flowing; and out of it like wind along the waste, not knowing whither.

30.gloss: Hurried here without being asked, and hurried hence without being asked; many a cup of this forbidden wine must drown the memory of that insolence.

31.gloss: From earth's centre I rose through the seventh gate to the throne of Saturn and unravelled many knots on the road, but not the master-knot of human fate.

32.gloss: There was a door to which I found no key and a veil through which I could not see; a little talk of me and thee, and then no more of thee and me.

33.gloss: Earth could not answer, nor the seas mourning in purple for their lost lord, nor rolling heaven with all its signs revealed and hidden by night and morning.

34.gloss: Seeking the thee-in-me that works behind the veil, I lifted my hands for a lamp in the darkness and heard, as from outside: the me within thee is blind.

35.gloss: I leaned to the lip of the poor earthen urn to learn the secret of my life, and lip to lip it murmured: drink while you live, for once dead you never return.

36.gloss: The vessel that answered with a fleeting voice once lived and drank; the passive lip I kissed, how many kisses it once took and gave.

37.gloss: I remember stopping to watch a potter thumping his wet clay, and with its obliterated tongue it murmured: gently, brother, gently, pray.

38.gloss: Has not such a story rolled down the generations of a clod of saturated earth cast by the Maker into human mould?

39.gloss: Not a drop we throw from our cups for earth to drink but may steal below to quench the fire of anguish in some eye hidden far beneath and long ago.

40.gloss: As the tulip looks up each morning for its heavenly vintage from the soil, do the same devoutly until heaven turns you over like an empty cup.

41.gloss: Perplexed no more with human or divine, resign tomorrow's tangle to the winds and lose your fingers in the tresses of the cypress-slender cup-bearer.

42.gloss: If the wine you drink and the lip you press end in what all begins and ends in, then you are today what you were yesterday, and tomorrow you shall be no less.

43.gloss: When the angel of the darker drink finds you at last by the river brink and offers his cup, inviting your soul forth to your lips, you shall not shrink.

44.gloss: If the soul can fling the dust aside and ride naked on the air of heaven, is it not a shame for it to stay crippled in this clay carcass?

45.gloss: Life is but a tent where a sultan bound for the realm of death rests one day; the sultan rises and the dark servant strikes it, preparing it for another guest.

46.gloss: Do not fear that existence, closing your account and mine, will know nothing like us again; the eternal cup-bearer has poured millions of bubbles like us from that bowl and will pour more.

47.gloss: When you and I have passed behind the veil, the world will last a long, long while, heeding our coming and departure as the sea heeds a pebble cast into it.

48.gloss: A moment's halt, a momentary taste of being from the well amid the waste, and the phantom caravan has reached the nothing it set out from: make haste.

49.gloss: Would you spend your spangle of existence on the secret? Then be quick about it, friend: a hair perhaps divides the false from the true, and on what does life depend?

50.gloss: A hair perhaps divides the false and true, and a single alif might be the clue, could you but find it, to the treasure-house and perhaps to the Master too.

51.gloss: His secret presence runs quicksilver-like through creation's veins, eluding your pains and taking all shapes from moon to fish; they all change and perish, but He remains.

52.gloss: A moment guessed, then back behind the fold of darkness rolled around the drama which He Himself contrives, enacts and beholds for the pastime of eternity.

53.gloss: If you gaze in vain today, while you are you, at the stubborn floor of earth and heaven's unopening door, how then tomorrow, when you shall be you no more?

54.gloss: Waste not your hour in the vain pursuit and dispute of this and that; better be merry with the fruitful grape than sadden after no fruit or bitter fruit.

55.gloss: With a brave carouse I made a second marriage in my house, divorced old barren reason from my bed and took the daughter of the vine to spouse.

56.gloss: Though I define is and is-not by rule and line and up-and-down by logic, of all one should care to fathom I was never deep in anything but wine.

57.gloss: People say my computations reduced the year to a better reckoning; it was only striking from the calendar unborn tomorrow and dead yesterday.

58.gloss: Lately, by the tavern door at dusk, an angel shape came shining through bearing a vessel on his shoulder and bid me taste of it: it was the grape.

59.gloss: The grape that with absolute logic confutes the seventy-two jarring sects, the sovereign alchemist that in a trice transmutes life's leaden metal into gold.

60.gloss: The mighty Mahmud, lord breathing God's name, scatters before him with his whirlwind sword the black horde of fears and sorrows that infest the soul.

61.gloss: If this juice is the growth of God, who dares blaspheme the twisted tendril as a snare? If a blessing, we should use it; if a curse, who set it there?

62.gloss: Must I abjure the balm of life, scared by some after-reckoning taken on trust or lured by hope of some diviner drink, to fill the cup only when crumbled into dust?

63.gloss: Of threats of hell and hopes of paradise, one thing at least is certain: this life flies; one thing is certain and the rest is lies; the flower that once has blown forever dies.

64.gloss: Strange that of the myriads who passed through the door of darkness before us, not one returns to tell us of the road which we too must travel to discover.

65.gloss: The revelations of the devout and learned who rose before us and burned as prophets are only stories which, awake from sleep, they told their comrades before returning to sleep.

66.gloss: I sent my soul through the invisible to spell some letter of the afterlife, and by and by my soul returned and answered: I myself am heaven and hell.

67.gloss: Heaven is but the vision of fulfilled desire and hell the shadow of a soul on fire, cast on the darkness we so lately emerged from and shall so soon re-enter.

68.gloss: We are no other than a moving row of magic shadow-shapes that come and go round the sun-lit lantern held at midnight by the master of the show.

69.gloss: We are helpless pieces of the game He plays on the chequer-board of nights and days; He moves us hither and thither, checks and slays, and lays us one by one back in the closet.

70.gloss: The ball makes no question of ayes and noes but goes here or there as the player strikes; and He who tossed you down into the field knows about it all.

71.gloss: The moving finger writes and, having written, moves on; neither your piety nor wit shall lure it back to cancel half a line, nor all your tears wash out a word of it.

72.gloss: That inverted bowl they call the sky, under which we crawl cooped up and live and die: lift not your hands to it for help, for it moves as impotently as you or I.

73.gloss: With earth's first clay they kneaded the last man and sowed there the seed of the last harvest; the first morning of creation wrote what the last dawn of reckoning shall read.

74.gloss: Yesterday prepared this day's madness and tomorrow's silence, triumph or despair; drink, for you know not whence you came nor why, drink, for you know not why you go nor where.

75.gloss: When heaven's foal was started from the goal and Parwin and Mushtari flung over its flaming shoulders, my predestined plot of dust and soul was fixed.

1.gloss: The sun casts the lasso of dawn over the roof and the king of day drops the die into the cup; drink wine, for the dawn-crier calls out to the days: drink.

2.gloss: A call came at dawn from our tavern: rise, mad reveller of the ruins, and let us fill the cup with wine before our own cup of life is filled.

3.gloss: It is dawn, rise, my graceful one; drink wine little by little and play the harp, for those who are here will not stay long and those who have gone never return.

4.gloss: Now that the world lies within reach of joy, every living heart longs for the open country; on every branch the hand of Moses appears and in every breath the breath of Jesus.

5.gloss: The drunken nightingale found its way into the garden, saw the laughing face of the rose and the cup of wine, and whispered in my ear: seize the moment, for a life gone by cannot be found again.

6.gloss: A fine day, neither hot nor cold; the cloud washes the dust from the face of the rose garden, and the nightingale cries to the yellow rose that wine must be drunk.

7.gloss: Fill a cup of the wine that gives life a second life, even if it costs you a headache; put it in my hand, for the world's work is a fable and life passes with every breath.

8.gloss: At the morning draught, fortunate idol, make a song and bring wine; the coming of autumn and going of winter has thrown a hundred thousand Jams and Kays to the dust.

9.gloss: While bone, vein and sinew are in your body, do not step outside the house of fate; bow your neck to no tyrant though he be Rustam son of Zal, and accept no favour though the giver be Hatim of Tayy.

10.gloss: Take up cup and jug, my sweet, and sit at ease in the field by the stream; many a dear person the ill-tempered wheel of heaven has turned a hundred times into cup and a hundred times into jug.

11.gloss: A flask of ruby wine and a book of poems, a bare morsel and half a loaf, and you and I seated in some porch: a pleasure beyond the reach of any sultan.

12.gloss: People say paradise with its houris is sweet; I say the juice of the grape is sweet; take this cash and let go of that credit, for the sound of the drum is sweet only from afar.

13.gloss: The rose said: I came with a gold-scattering hand, laughing into the world; I untied the string of my purse and went, spending every coin I had.

14.gloss: My heart, suppose you had every good of the world and your garden of joy adorned with green; then count yourself a dewdrop that sat on that grass one night and rose at dawn.

15.gloss: Before they ambush you, order the rose-red wine; you are not gold, heedless fool, that once laid in the earth they would dig you out again.

16.gloss: This old caravanserai called the world, resting place of the piebald horse of morning and evening, is a feast left behind by a hundred Jamshids and a palace that pillowed a hundred Bahrams.

17.gloss: In the palace where Jamshid raised his cup, the gazelle has borne its young and the fox lies at rest; Bahram, who hunted the wild ass all his life, see how the grave has hunted Bahram.

18.gloss: Wherever there has been a bed of tulips, those tulips grew from the blood of a king; every violet leaf that rises from the earth was once a mole on a beauty's cheek.

19.gloss: Every blade of grass that grows by a stream grew as if from the lip of an angel-natured one; set no foot on the grass in scorn, for it grew from the dust of a tulip-cheeked beauty.

20.gloss: Friend, let us not grieve over tomorrow but count this one breath of life as our spoil; tomorrow, when we leave this old monastery, we travel with the wayfarers of seven thousand years.

21.gloss: Our congenial friends have all slipped from our hands, trampled one by one beneath the feet of death; we drank the same wine at the banquet of life, and they got drunk a round or two before us.

22.gloss: The cloud came and wept again over the grass; one must not live without rose-coloured wine; this grass is our spectacle today, and whose spectacle will the grass over our dust be?

23.gloss: Do not let grief embrace you, nor the sorrow and weariness of the days take hold of you; do not forsake your book, the stream-bank and the field before the earth embraces you.

24.gloss: One group ponders the path of religion, another is lost in doubt on the road to certainty; suddenly a crier will call from ambush: heedless ones, the way is neither this nor that.

25.gloss: Those who became oceans of learning and manners and lamps among their companions in uncovering the sciences found no road out of this dark night; they told a tale and fell asleep.

26.gloss: Drink wine, for you will sleep long beneath the clay without companion, friend or mate; tell no one this hidden secret: no tulip that has withered blooms again.

27.gloss: For a while in childhood we went to a teacher, for a while we rejoiced in our own mastery; hear how the tale ends: we came from dust and went with the wind.

28.gloss: I was a bird that flew from the world of mystery, hoping to rise from the low to the high; finding no one here who shared the secret, I went back out by the door I came in.

29.gloss: These two or three days of my turn at life have passed like water in a stream and wind over the plain; I never grieved over two days: the one not yet come and the one gone by.

30.gloss: Since my coming was not my choice on the first day, and this unwilling going is a settled matter, rise and gird yourself, nimble cup-bearer, for I will wash away the world's sorrow with wine.

31.gloss: From the depths of black clay to the height of Saturn I solved all the world's problems and loosed every hard knot by cunning; every knot came undone except the knot of death.

32.gloss: The secrets of eternity neither you nor I know, nor can either of us read this riddle; our talk of me and you goes on behind the curtain, and when the curtain falls neither you nor I remain.

33.gloss: The sky whispered secretly in my heart's ear: you know the decree that fate laid upon me; if I had any power over my own turning I would free myself from this bewilderment.

34.gloss: Out of great longing I put my lip to the lip of the jug to win from it the means of a long life; lip upon my lip it told me this secret: drink wine, for you will not come back to this world.

35.gloss: This jug was once a desperate lover like me, bound in the curl of some beauty's hair; the handle you see on its neck was once an arm around a sweetheart's neck.

36.gloss: Yesterday I saw a potter in the market kicking a lump of clay again and again; the clay said to him in its mute language: I was once like you, treat me kindly.

37.gloss: Do not recall the yesterday that has passed nor cry out for the tomorrow not yet come; build on neither the unarrived nor the gone; be happy for a moment and do not throw your life to the wind.

38.gloss: This caravan of life passes strangely; seize the moment that passes in joy; cup-bearer, why worry about tomorrow's resurrection? Bring the cup of wine, for the night is passing.

39.gloss: Those who became captives of reason and discernment wasted away grieving over being and not-being; go, you heedless one, choose the juice of the grape, for those heedless ones shrivelled from sour grapes into raisins.

40.gloss: Tonight I will make a cup of wine the size of a maund and enrich myself with two measures of it; first I will divorce reason and religion three times, then take the daughter of the vine to wife.

41.gloss: I know the outward of non-being and being and the inward of every height and depth; yet shame on my knowledge if I know any rank higher than drunkenness.

42.gloss: Drunk, I passed by the tavern last night and saw an old man drunk with a jug on his shoulder; I said, have you no shame before God? He said: God is generous, drink wine.

43.gloss: Drink wine, for it takes from the heart the thought of less and more and the anxieties of the seventy-two sects; do not abstain from the elixir of which one draught cures a thousand ills.

44.gloss: Sit with wine, for this is the kingdom of Mahmud; hear the harp, for this is the melody of David; think no more of what has come and gone; be happy now, for that is the purpose.

45.gloss: Better to flee from every lesson and science and cling to the curl of the beloved's hair; before time spills your blood, better to pour the flask's blood into the cup.

46.gloss: This wheel of heaven at which we stand bewildered is like a magic lantern we know of: the sun is the lamp, the world the lantern, and we are the figures turning within it in wonder.

47.gloss: Khayyam, if you are drunk with wine, be happy; if you sit with a moon-faced one, be happy; since the end of the world's affair is non-being, imagine you are nothing while you are, and be happy.

48.gloss: In the circle of the heavens whose depth none can fathom, drink wine gladly, for the turn comes round by turn; when your turn comes do not sigh; drink gladly, for it is turn-taking, not injustice.

49.gloss: We are puppets and heaven the puppeteer, in truth and not in metaphor; we play a while on the board of existence and fall one by one back into the box of non-being.

50.gloss: You who roll like a ball before the polo-stick of fate, go left or right and say nothing; the one who set you running knows, He knows, He knows, and He.

51.gloss: The signs of all that would be were there from the start; the pen has written good and bad without pause; what had to be was given in destiny; our grieving and striving are in vain.

52.gloss: The good and evil in human nature, the joy and grief in fate and destiny: do not blame the wheel of heaven, for on the road of reason the wheel is a thousand times more helpless than you.

53.gloss: Be happy, for they settled your affairs yesterday and freed themselves of your wishes yesterday; what can I say? Without your asking, yesterday they fixed the resting place of your tomorrow.

54.gloss: On the day they saddled the steed of heaven and adorned Jupiter and the Pleiades, this was our share from the court of fate; what is our sin? Our lot was fixed thus.

55.gloss: When the eternal generosity created me, it first dictated to me the lesson of love; then it made the scattered filings of my heart a key to the treasuries of meaning.

56.gloss: If I tell you the secret in the tavern, it is better than praying without you in the prayer niche; you who are the first and the last of all creation, burn me if you will or cherish me.

57.gloss: You set a thousand snares on my path and say you will seize me if I take a step; not an atom of the world is empty of your command; you command me, and then you name me a sinner.

58.gloss: I am a sinful servant; where is your good pleasure? My heart is dark; where is your light and purity? If you grant me paradise for obedience, that is wages; where then are your grace and gift?

59.gloss: The day before yesterday I passed a potter who showed a new art from clay at every moment; I saw, though the blind did not, my father's dust in the hand of every potter.

60.gloss: Last night I went into the potters' workshop and saw two thousand jugs, speaking and silent; suddenly one jug cried out: where is the potter, the jug-buyer and the jug-seller?

61.gloss: The joined pieces of a cup: how could even a drunkard allow it to be broken? So many lovely heads, hands and feet were joined in love; by whose hatred were they broken?

62.gloss: A cup that reason praises and kisses a hundred times on the brow with love: this potter of time makes such a delicate cup and smashes it again on the ground.

63.gloss: When the Creator arranged the mixture of the elements, why did he cast it into deficiency? If the form came out good, why break it? And if it did not come out good, whose fault is the flaw?

64.gloss: They say there will be paradise and houris, and there pure wine and honey; if we have chosen wine and a beloved here, what fear, since the end will be the same?

65.gloss: When the sapling of my life is uprooted and my parts are scattered, let them make a flask from my clay; when you fill it with wine it will come alive again.

66.gloss: The month of Ramadan has passed and Shawwal has come, the season of joy, pleasure and minstrels; the time has come when wineskins on shoulders say: the porter has come, back to back.

67.gloss: Beware, strengthen me with the cup of wine and make this amber face like ruby; when I die, wash me with wine and make the boards of my coffin from the wood of the vine.

68.gloss: I will drink so much wine that its scent rises from the earth when I am beneath it, so that a reveller passing over my dust becomes drunk and ruined from the scent of my wine.

69.gloss: Had my coming been up to me I would not have come, and had my ceasing been up to me, when would I cease? Better still if in this ruined monastery I had neither come nor been nor gone.

70.gloss: Every day I resolve to repent at night, to repent of the cup and the brimming bowl; now that the time of roses has come, do not abandon it; in the season of roses, Lord, I repent of repentance.

71.gloss: Since Venus and the moon appeared in the sky, no one has seen anything better than pure wine; I marvel at the wine-sellers: what could they buy that is better than what they sell?

72.gloss: Alas, the book of youth is closed and that fresh spring of life is over; that bird of joy whose name was youth, alas, I do not know when it came or when it went.

73.gloss: If I had power over the heavens like God, I would remove this heaven from the midst and build another anew, so that the free might easily reach their heart's desire.

74.gloss: Moonlight has split the skirt of night with its glow; drink wine, for no moment better than this can be found; be happy and do not brood, for the moon will shine long on each of our dust one by one.

75.gloss: Friends, when you meet together, rejoice in one another; when the cup-bearer takes the Magian wine in hand, remember poor so-and-so with a prayer.
